items.title: Diagnosis confidence is low
items.body: The model isn’t sure whether the repeated sign error is a genuine misconception or a careless slip. Her self-reported reason ("silly mistake") conflicts with a three-time pattern. Your read would settle it.
items.asks: Is this a real gap or a slip?

items.label: Q1
items.note: Wrote 3x = 11 − 7. Sign not flipped when moving −7 across =.

items.label: Q3
items.note: Wrote 5x = 16 − 4. Same sign error as Q1.

items.label: Q5
items.note: Lost the sign on −2x. Flagged as "silly mistake" — the point of contention.

items.title: Answering "I don’t know" to skip
items.body: Daniel selected "I don’t know" on 4 of 6 diagnostic prompts in a row, which reads as skipping the diagnostic rather than engaging with it. Credit has been withheld pending your view.
items.asks: Nudge in person, or let the system re-prompt?

items.label: P2
items.note: Selected "I don’t know" without an attempt.

items.label: P3
items.note: "I don’t know" again — 2nd in a row.

items.label: P5
items.note: "I don’t know" — 4th. Reads as skipping, not stuck.

items.title: Probe may have cued the answer
items.body: A probe-mode question was phrased in a way that could have hinted the correct step, so the "understood" result here may be softer than it looks. Flagged so it isn’t over-weighted.

items.label: Probe
items.note: The phrasing itself hints the correct order — the "yes" may not reflect real understanding.

items.label: Check
items.note: Correct, but immediately after the cue.

items.title: Mastery vs. retention mismatch
items.body: Same-session accuracy is high, but delayed retrieval two weeks on dropped sharply. The model is unsure whether to keep this topic marked mastered.
items.asks: Hold at mastered, or schedule extra review?

items.label: Now
items.note: 3 of 5 — the drop the model is unsure how to weight.
